title: Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc
description: The core package for building MVC web applications and APIs with ASP.NET Core.

data.text: Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc provides the framework for building web applications using the Model-View-Controller pattern. It includes routing, model binding, validation, filters, and API versioning.

data.title: Creating a Controller

terms.definition: An attribute that enables API-specific behaviors like automatic model validation.
The process of converting HTTP request data into .NET objects.

data.title: Tip
data.text: Use `[ApiController]` for REST APIs and `[Controller]` for MVC views.
Routing, Model Binding, and Action Results

MVC maps an incoming URL to a controller action through routing, binds request data to action parameters, and returns an action result the framework writes to the response. Attribute routing puts the template next to the action, so the endpoint shape is visible where it is implemented.

data.title: A controller with validation and typed results
Interview angle: the filter pipeline
data.text: A request passes through middleware, then routing, then model binding, then filters — authorization, resource, action — then the action, then result filters. Knowing where to put cross-cutting logic matters: validation and exception handling belong in filters or middleware, not in every action. This is the answer that separates someone who has used MVC from someone who has debugged it.

data.title: Key Takeaways
data.takeaway: Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc is the foundation for web apps and APIs in ASP.NET Core.
